question.problem:
The dimensions of a rectangular floor are $12\,\text{m}\times 3\,\text{m}$, where each dimension is measured to the nearest $1\,\text{m}.$ Rounded to the nearest square meter, what is the smallest possible area of the floor?

To the nearest square meter, the smallest possible area is
{{field-1}}${\text{m}}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
Each dimension is given to the nearest $1\,\text{m}.$ So, the greatest possible error of these measurements is

$$
\frac{1\,\text{m}}{2}=0.5\,\text{m}.
$$

We wish to find the *smallest* possible area of the container. Therefore, we require the *lower bound* of each dimension.

The lower bounds for each dimension are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & 12\,\text{m}-0.5\,\text{m}=11.5\,\text{m} \\  & 3\,\text{m}-0.5\,\text{m}=2.5\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the smallest possible area of the container is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =11.5\,\text{m}\times 2.5\,\text{m} \\  & =28.75\,{\text{m}}^{2} \\  & ≈29\,{\text{m}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest square meter.
